results.title: Making AI Work: Nebius Increases AI Cloud Pricing as Demand for Computing Power Surges, ETEnterpriseai
highlights:
On-demand rates for some central processing units, made by AMD and Intel, and memory offerings have also been hiked.

Cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected Nvidia chips from October 1, marking the company's second price hike in three months. Demand for computing capacity to train and run AI models is surging; rival CoreWeave said earlier in the day that it is signing contracts at higher prices. Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between 17 per cent and 21 per cent. On-demand rates for some central processing units, made by AMD and Intel, and memory offerings have also been hiked. 

Prices of some CPU-only instances will rise by 25 per cent and those of memory offerings by about 41 per cent, the company said. The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm said that customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive commitment discounts. Nebius' price increases follow a quarter of rapid growth in its AI cloud business, as the company signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each. Neocloud firms like Nebius rent out high-powered chips and data centre infrastructure needed for AI models.

results.title: GPU shortage pushes enterprises to rethink hybrid cloud for AI workloads
highlights:
Enterprises trying to scale artificial intelligence (AI) workloads are running into a hardware market where graphics processing units (GPUs) are effectively rationed and colocation space is increasingly reserved for the largest cloud providers.

That scarcity is reshaping infrastructure planning. Some companies are stockpiling capacity before they know what they will use it for, while others discover late in the process that they lack the power or cooling to run what they have already committed to build.

“All capacities, all GPU cards, are running at full scale, so none are wasted,” said Yitian Xu, head of solutions for Alibaba Cloud’s UK and Ireland, Nordics and Cyprus region. “All customers who want to deploy GPU cards have to wait.”

Xu said customers now have to commit to one- or two-year contracts to reserve capacity, as demand from both external customers and Alibaba Cloud’s own internal model use keeps climbing. He linked the strain to a wider constraint: the UK’s limited electricity supply, which he called a national growth problem.

Retika Gupta, a solutions architect at Enterprise Rent-A-Car, said buying GPUs has become difficult for the same reason. Suppliers routinely quote six to 12 months for delivery, she said, and the timeline can shift again after an order is placed.

She said the uncertainty raises a harder question before any purchase: whether it is worth buying high-capacity GPUs at all, given they are likely to be outdated within 18 months, rather than leaning on cloud capacity or existing infrastructure instead.

results.title: 数据显微镜｜再涨20％：GPU租金二度上调，算力缺口仍在拉大_腾讯新闻
highlights:
9月17日，云计算服务提供商Nebius向客户发出调价通知，拟自10月1日起上调主要英伟达 GPU的按需(on-demand)租金：H100由每小时3.85美元升至4.50美元，H200由4.50美元升至5.40美元，B200由7.15美元升至8.50美元，B300由7.85美元升至9.50美元，本轮涨幅约17%至21%。

这已是该公司年内第二次全面上调按需价格。若按两轮公开报价计算，以其首轮调价前的6.10美元为起点，B300每小时租金年内累计涨幅已达约56%。

价格连续上行的另一面，是算力供需缺口仍在拉大。中国信通院数据显示，2026年一季度，国内AI算力需求同比增长417%，同期有效供给增速仅为128%。从海外按需报价到国内合同金额，价格上行的链条正被逐段验证。

...

本轮调价并非孤立事件。今年5月宣布、6月1日生效的一轮提价中，Nebius已将H100由2.95美元/小时升至3.85美元，H200由3.50美元升至4.50美元，B200由5.50美元升至7.15美元，B300由6.10美元升至7.85美元，整体涨幅约29%。两轮叠加，Nebius自身报价序列的绝对水平因此被逐轮抬升。

...

更能说明紧张程度的是，涨价范围已溢出加速卡本身。同批调整中，纯CPU计算的AMD EPYC Genoa由0.012美元/vCPU小时上调25%至0.015美元，Genoa内存由0.0032美元/GiB小时上调约41%至0.0045美元，供给偏紧不只发生在GPU一隅，而是覆盖了算力基础设施的多个环节。

半导体行业的长期惯例是芯片出厂即开始贬值，如今这一规律在算力租赁环节出现了反转。英伟达官方口径印证了这一趋势：据英伟达首席财务官Colette Kress在2026财年第二季度财报电话会上的表述，Hopper系列GPU的租赁价格年内累计上涨20%，上一代的A100云价上涨近15%。

...

中国信通院的数据为这场涨价提供了最直接的注脚：2026年一季度，国内AI算力需求同比增长417%，而有效供给增速仅为128%。两个数字相除，需求增速约为供给增速的3.3倍。

缺口难以短期弥合，与算力基础设施建设节奏有关。开源证券在研报中提及，传统数据中心建设周期长达三年以上，从选址、审批、土建到设备进场、调试上架，每一环都难以压缩；而AI模型与应用的迭代以季度为单位。供需两端时间尺度不一致，直接催生了对“按需付费、弹性扩容”这类轻资产模式的旺盛需求。

规模数据印证了这一点。中国信通院数据显示，2026年一季度国内算力租赁市场规模达680亿元，同比增长62%，全年预计突破2600亿元。IDC的预测更为宏观：2026年全球算力租赁市场规模将突破800亿美元，年复合增长率超过25%。租赁正从临时的补位方案，变成算力供给体系中的常规组成部分。

...

浙商证券将这一变化概括为定价逻辑的切换：2026年上半年，算力租赁板块的定价核心是供给端的拿卡能力，市场交易的是“谁能拿到GPU”；进入当前阶段，定价权正向需求端切换，市场开始验证“客户是否愿意为算力付更多钱”。国内算力租赁价格上调，已经进入公告验证阶段。

...

缺口扩大，不等于供给停滞。工业和信息化部8月26日在国新办新闻发布会上介绍，截至2026年6月底，我国智能算力规模达2185 EFLOPS，同比增长177%；围绕算力枢纽已建成70余条算力大通道，全国算力设施整体上架率达71.4%。

...

不过，供给端的约束依然真实。据公开报道，台积电的先进制程产能已被英伟达等大客户锁定，预计到2027年上半年仍暂无缓解迹象；HBM高带宽内存供应持续偏紧，高端AI服务器的整机交付周期因此拉长。开源证券判断，受先进封装产能限制，高端GPU的供需紧平衡状态或将贯穿2026年全年。换言之，算力价格的支撑并非短期扰动，而是产能建设的物理节奏所致。

results.title: 404K SEMI-AI: M7 & CSP Weekly (2026-09-18) — Firming Rental Rates: Hyperscalers Accelerate Expansion; Focus Shifts to Delivery and Cash Collections Next Week
highlights:
Cloud compute rental rates and booking momentum remained firm this week, but capacity expansion bottlenecks are increasingly concentrated in power interconnection, project financing, and customer payment terms. While Alphabet (Google) and Amazon seek returns on proprietary silicon, Microsoft emphasizes customer diversification. For neo-cloud providers, translating capacity shortages into hard cash flow depends on executing physical deliveries, sustaining high utilization, and securing viable financing structures simultaneously.

...

Cloud compute demand remains robust, but the lag between securing bookings and realizing cash collections is widening. Across the board—from Google's commentary on custom silicon payback periods and Microsoft's push to build compute for a broader enterprise base, to late-week price hikes and funding announcements by neo-clouds—the core question converges: can demand translate into collectible service revenue quickly enough after upfront hardware capital outlays?

The most tangible shift on the demand side is pricing power. Nebius plans to raise on-demand pricing on select GPUs effective October 1; CoreWeave reported higher realized rates on recent short-term contracts; and IREN management stated that its 2026 capacity is fully sold out. Spanning on-demand rates, short-term commitments, and bulk capacity sales, these signals reaffirm that near-term deliverable compute remains tight—though they cannot be mechanically extrapolated into sector-wide revenue growth.

Supply-side friction is also crystallizing. Custom silicon faces manufacturing and advanced packaging lead times; data centers must secure power interconnection and complete construction; and clusters require substantial funding before generating operational revenue. Google's reported involvement in Crux AI's financing, CoreWeave's proposed debt and equity capital raise, and Amazon linking backup generator procurement to equity warrants all illustrate that capacity expansion is simultaneously testing procurement, financing structures, and physical execution.

...

The investment thesis remains two-sided: near-term scarcity bolsters rental rates and order books, yet massive upfront capital expenditures do not automatically guarantee attractive returns. If premium pricing is confined to limited short-term deals, or if customers trade higher nominal rates for lower upfront prepayments, an apparent uplift in revenue visibility may actually widen funding deficits. Next week, investors should scrutinize delivery schedules and contractual payment terms before factoring in expansion returns.

...

Specific customer interviews highlighted compute commitments lengthening from one to three years, accompanied by mandatory 30% to 40% upfront prepayments. While these terms reflect idiosyncratic contracts rather than a universal industry standard, they underscore a critical demand-side constraint: willingness to consume compute does not guarantee the balance-sheet liquidity required to lock in capacity. Evaluating the foundation model sector requires assessing product ARR alongside procurement cash flow terms.

...

Nebius's rate hikes provide an unambiguous signal of near-term spot capacity tightness, though revenue realization lies ahead. Media reports outline the following on-demand GPU pricing adjustments planned by Nebius, effective October 1. Because hardware specifications and service configurations differ across generations, the table evaluates only the delta between old and new prices for each respective GPU model, rather than asserting cross-architecture price-to-performance rankings.

Nebius Select GPU On-Demand Pricing Hikes (Effective Oct 1; Utilization Subject to Post-Implementation Verification)

Increases in on-demand rack rates do not trigger immediate repricing across existing long-term contracted capacity. Top-line impact depends on the proportion of spot customers, billable instance hours, and customer retention post-hike; if clients curtail runtime hours in response, nominal price increases will be diluted. Similarly, CoreWeave's disclosed annualized pricing on short-term contracts reflects clearing prices under specific duration and delivery windows, which should not be conflated with the blended average selling price (ASP) of its entire fleet over multi-year horizons.

...

A structural duration mismatch exists between short-term spot price spikes and long-lived datacenter assets. Clusters must operate over multi-year lifecycles, and once short-term tenancies expire, operators face potentially softer supply-demand dynamics and tighter capital markets. Consequently, near-term firming in realized rates should inform near-term revenue projections, while long-term ROIC demands durable multi-year tenant retention, manageable hardware upgrade cycles, and viable debt refinancing conditions.

...

The primary debate in cloud compute is whether acute near-term shortages can justify mounting forward capital commitments. The bull thesis leans on pricing power, expanding order backlogs, compressed in-house silicon payback cycles, and broadening enterprise workload penetration. The bear thesis cautions that elevated spot rates are transitory, forward datacenter construction is draining liquidity, and foundation model clients are buckling under unsustainable compute bills. Both dynamics can coexist; distinguishing between them requires tracking GAAP revenue conversion and customer cash payment cadence.

On 16 September, OpenAI PVT$1.18T — OpenAI, private, latest valuation $1.18T disclosed six new "concerning" misalignment incidents (agents inventing data, hiding mistakes, uploading code to the internet without permission) along with a framework for reporting more↗ 6. If bookings hold at the new card, scarcity is confirmed and asset-backed finance gets cheaper to roll forward. One warning light I could not check: bears cite secondhand accelerator prices as the earliest signal of capex trouble, and no published index I could reach this week carries that number: the organized market for used GPUs↗ itself only opened on 17 July 10. results.title: A.I. Data Centers and the Future of Distributed Compute | Observer
highlights:
The A.I. boom has concentrated compute in enormous data centers, but advances in distributed training are challenging the assumption that serious A.I. workloads must live in hyperscale campuses. Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images

...

Electricity impacts are wider, yet still bounded by the reach of the regional grid operator. Electricity bills for households hundreds of miles from any server hall carry a similar imprint. Data center demand drove 63 percent of one year’s capacity price increase across the 13-state PJM grid region, or about $9.3 billion recovered from ratepayers, including households and small businesses.

...

Several forces pull operators toward enormous single sites, from power contracts to construction economics. But those constraints can be overcome. They mainly raise costs, and paying more to spread the chips can look like a reasonable trade once local objections, grid limits and permitting are counted. The binding constraint on the largest sites is the training of new models. That one is closer to binary: either there is enough capacity to train a model at the next scale, or there isn’t.

Training a frontier model has typically required thousands of high-end GPUs packed into a single facility. The algorithms that train these models depend on constant synchronization, with chips exchanging updates at every training step. That traffic demands ultra-low latency and massive bandwidth, which traditionally exist only inside one tightly networked building. That is why A.I. data centers have grown so large, and why they are now pressing against the physical limits of how many chips can sit in one place.

results.title: The price of computing power shifts from "scarcity" to "reporting": domestic computing power synchronously releases perf… | Longbridge
highlights:
Affected by the rise of AI and semiconductor stocks in the US market and the systematic increase in computing power rental prices, computing power assets in both the A-share and Hong Kong markets have become active across the board. Stocks of giants like NVIDIA have risen, and Jensen Huang expects chip sales to double next year. European cloud provider Nebius has raised prices again, tightening business terms, and the supply-demand imbalance in computing power is reflected in financial statements. Funds are flowing back into the South Korean stock market, and Morgan Stanley has upgraded its rating. The global technology industry chain's risk appetite is recovering, and domestic computing power is simultaneously ramping up to deliver performance

...

More noteworthy than the indices is the systematic upward shift in the central price of computing power leasing. European cloud computing provider Nebius announced another price increase effective October 1st, with GPU rental rates rising by 17% to 21%, and the cumulative increase for B300 reaching about 56% within the year, marking its second price hike in three months; during the same period, CoreWeave signed a short-term contract for the third quarter at a high price of about $40 million/MW, with over $25 billion in new customer net commitments added at the beginning of the quarter. A more structural change is the tightening of business terms—computing power procurement is shifting from "reserving for one year" to "reserving for three years," with the prepayment ratio raised to 30% to 40%. The three factors of price, duration, and prepayment are all tilting towards the suppliers, indicating that the narrative of "supply not meeting demand" has transformed into quantifiable figures in financial reports.

...

Domestic GPUs are the direction with the greatest demand elasticity. Tianzu Zhixin (09903) rose 7.09% during the day, reporting HKD 134.40, up 178.84% year-to-date. Behind this is the combination of the rising slope of domestic model token consumption and accelerated adaptation of chip models: domestic GPUs have completed inference optimization for mainstream models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, coupled with overseas supply constraints and the lagging pace of domestic capacity expansion, leading to a continuous widening of the supply-demand gap.

Computing power operations represent the area of certain premium. Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Intelligent Computing (01396) rose 2.41% during the day, reporting HKD 11.47 (as of press time), with a cumulative increase of 133.26% year-to-date. Similarly facing a shortage of computing power, overseas neocloud has realized the scarcity into hourly rental fees by "raising prices"; Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Intelligent Computing relies on "long-term contracts"— as of mid-2026, the intended computing power technology service orders on hand exceed RMB 37 billion (with delivered and stable billing scale exceeding RMB 20 billion), and over 95% of the new signed orders this year are long-term contracts of three to five years, turning scarcity into certain cash flow. The hardware segment earns from the prosperity beta, while the operations segment earns from the certain premium locked in by long-term contracts.
